hits.story_text:
While moving around, I really missed my mechanical keyboard at home. It's kinda calm feeling of keys - clacking while i am aggressively addressing my agents.

That's when I came up with Clacketier. Open-source package to add mechanical keyboard sounds to any supported MacOS terminal: https://github.com/vipulgupta2048/clacketier

Currently supports: Cherry MX Blue, Brown and Red switches.

Will be maintianing this going forward as I use it more. Tried a few alternatives too but feel they are either lagging way too much, way too heavy or not having the right support. Clacketier can play sounds per key with afplay in under 1ms.

Features incoming: 1. Acuation point adjustments 2. Add your keyboard sound by switches 3. Support more application beyond the terminal

hits.story_text:
Woodada is a free desktop app for windows and mac. Two cats, one for CPU and one for memory, run along your taskbar or Dock. The busier your computer gets, the faster they run.

I loved RunCat but wanted the cat actually running across my screen, where I'd notice it. The cat sprites come from RunCat365 (Apache 2.0).

I built it with C#, .NET 9 and Avalonia, with help from AI. Just run the .exe or open the .dmg. As the cats run they collect fish, which you can spend on new colors and skins.

The app isn't code-signed yet, so you'll see a warning the first time you open it. VirusTotal results are on the homepage: https://hyuntae-jeong.github.io/Woodada/

I'd love your feedback!

hits.author: mattw2121
hits.story_text:
I made this game just for the fun of it and was hoping some of you might find it fun as well. It's a daily game where you need to analyze data from public sources and then set toggles before the daily cut off. The goal is to get all the toggles right and be able to maintain them.

I have an open beta starting November 30th to work out any kinks before the first official season starts on January 4th.

The example on the front page gives you an idea of how the toggles work. When you "lock" each day you are simulating what the system will do each day at 23:00 UTC. After locking the demo/example it also shows you what the data was behind the toggle, though you won't see that in the real game since the point is to figure it out :)

As the game progresses, it will drop hints for toggles in case you are having a hard time figuring out their source.

I actually did a one time run of this game (much more basic than it is today) 2-3 years ago and received a lot of positive feedback, so decided to rebuild it into something that could run over and over with multiple seasons.

Would really appreciate any feedback!
hits.title: Show HN: Toggles, Data Analysis Game

hits.story_text:
My wife is a piano teacher, and she often encounters a simple problem: students return home after their lessons and forget how a piece is supposed to sound or how a particular passage should be played.

I built Sheetlytic, an app that turns a photo of sheet music into playable music.

The idea is to bridge the gap between reading sheet music and hearing it, without having to search for an existing recording or manually enter notes into notation software.

While the original motivation came from piano teaching, I think it could also be useful for musicians learning unfamiliar pieces on their own.

Sheetlytic is available on:

Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=verbosus.sheetlytic

iOS: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/sheet-music-scanner-player/id6830832313

Windows: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9p2pm166vc69

I'm the developer and would love to hear your feedback, particularly on usability, recognition accuracy, and potential use cases.

Happy to answer any questions!
hits.title: Sheetlytic – Take a photo of sheet music and hear it play

hits.author: davidnashdev
hits.story_text:
Hey HN, I built* HIIT Builder (https://hiitbuilder.app) because I don't want to get fat. Truly I could just stop there.

But for more context, I got tired of hunting for YouTube workout videos that have both good routines and decent music. Turns out most YT workout creators, even the massive ones who could afford a license, have terrible music. So, fk it, I'll build my own workout generator and play my own Spotify playlists instead.

So far workouts have been completed across 13 countries (US, Iraq, Bangladesh, Austria, France, Germany, Brazil, Ukraine, Turkey, Netherlands, Spain, Chile, Australia), and someone in the Faroe Islands, either physically or maybe just their VPN, started one too.

A few technical details that might be interesting to my fellow nerds here:

After a few ugly first prototypes for the stick figures, I ended up using the strategy of modeling every animation as a compact 34-number pose vector (joint angles, abduction, etc.) like a 3D skeleton, then projecting it to a 2D SVG. That way any move can be rendered at any angle without having to re-do any major work.

For workout order, instead of pure random shuffles the routine builder runs simulated annealing over a fixed standing/floor block shape. This makes it so that trips to the floor are limited and muscle groups are rotated logically. Rest time is actually rest instead of using that time to get up or get down off the floor constantly.

Since one of my main concerns was bringing your own music, there are no audio files at all. I did add countdown beeps though with synthesized chonky square waves so they cut through Spotify.

*Full disclosure: Using 'built' nowadays is a dividing term lol. I used AI to write all the code for it. And while I've spent many hours reviewing and tweaking poses over and over until the form cues actually looked right, a few of the moves still have noticeable quirks that AI is bad at noticing. If you spot any weird ones let me know.
hits.title: Show HN: No-equipment workout generator with 3D-to-2D SVG figures
